title: Perf Lab: H200 Provisioning Plan (Infra/SRE)
body:
Owner: Sean (SRE)
Last reviewed with: Rina (bench harness), Connor (release), Noah (perf arch)

Purpose
- Add NVIDIA H200 capacity to Redwood perf-lab for the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint.
- Requirements: repeatable environments, low noise (minimal contention), auditable access, and enough quota to run the benchmark matrix (model x quant mode x workload preset) within 48–72 hrs.

Scope
- Provision H200 nodes into perf-lab cluster with a pinned “golden” base image and a locked benchmark runtime container.
- Integrate into existing reservation / scheduling mechanism (perf-lab allocator) so we can guarantee exclusive access during benchmark windows.
- Add minimal observability + safety rails (DCGM, clocks/power validation, node health checks).

Non-goals
- Production fleet rollout of H200 for customer traffic (this is perf-lab only).
- Multi-tenancy across many teams; initial access is a controlled allowlist.

Target capacity (initial)
- Phase 1 (sprint): 2 nodes online + 2 nodes staged (spares / burn-in)
- Phase 2 (post-sprint): 8 nodes total if the matrix and canary coverage expand

Assumptions / hardware notes
- Node class: HGX H200 (8x H200 SXM) “benchmark” nodes (no MIG)
- Network: 400Gb IB or equivalent (depending on rack availability); note that most benchmarking is single-node inference, but we want IB available for any future multi-GPU scaling tests and NCCL sanity.
- Storage: local NVMe scratch for datasets + traces; results artifacts uploaded immediately (don’t treat local disks as durable).
- MIG: disabled for all perf-lab GPU nodes (H100/H200) to reduce variability and simplify accounting.

Timeline (working)
Week -1 (now)
- Confirm allocation/quota + procurement status with infra ops (rack space, power budget).
- Confirm which benchmarks need H200 specifically (FP8 attention + long-context regression work).
- Finalize image + driver/CUDA stack (see “Golden image” section).

Week 1 (provision + burn-in)
- Bring up 2 nodes in perf-lab: join cluster, validate GPU enumeration, firmware levels, BIOS settings.
- Run burn-in:
  - GPU: dcgmproftester / cuda_memtest
  - Host: stress-ng, disk throughput sanity
  - Network: ib_write_bw / latency test if IB present
- Enable perf-lab allocator reservations for “h200” pool.

Week 2 (scale + gate)
- Add 2 additional nodes (total 4) if burn-in passes.
- Add a nightly perf-canary job subset on H200 (quant-perf): 1–2 model/workload presets only (keep it stable).

Risks / schedule threats
- Rack/power delays: if we can’t rack H200 quickly, fallback is to run partial matrix on H100 and treat H200 as “follow-up validation.”
- Driver/CUDA mismatch causing kernel path differences vs H100: we need pinned versions and to log them into artifacts.
- Node contention/noise: without strict reservation/exclusive access, results won’t be defensible. This is the main operational risk.

Quotas / reservation model
- We will treat H200 nodes as a separate resource pool: perf-lab/h200.
- Reservation granularity: 2-hour blocks, with a max of 24 hours per team per week during sprint (exceptions by Sean/Allison).
- During the benchmarking sprint matrix runs: reserve 2 nodes for the benchmark harness pipeline (Rina/Noah) and keep 1 node as “interactive profiling” (Grace/Yuki/Isabella) when available.
- Node allocation rules:
  - “Exclusive GPU” always (no sharing on the node).
  - One job per node unless explicitly marked multi-process (e.g., profiling + collector).

Golden image + software pinning
Goal: isolate performance variation to runtime changes, not image drift.

Base OS
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- Kernel: pinned (do not float) for the sprint window (exact version TBD once nodes arrive; capture in run artifacts)

NVIDIA stack (proposed)
- NVIDIA Driver: 550.54.15 (or the closest validated for H200 in our lab)
- CUDA: 12.4 toolkit runtime available in base, but prefer containerized CUDA for benchmark runs
- NCCL: pinned version aligned with CUDA (again, containerized where possible)
- DCGM: enabled for health + metrics

Containerization
- Benchmark runs must use pinned container digests (not tags).
- Use the perf-lab runtime build target (see GitHub redwood PR 10626) with metadata stamping:
  - runtime_commit
  - build flags
  - compiler versions
  - container_digest
- Store container digests in the benchmark config schema (see benchmark-lab PR 412) and record them in artifacts.

BIOS / firmware / power settings (must be documented per node)
- GPU persistence mode: ON
- GPU application clocks: locked to known-good values (recorded). If we can’t lock, we must record actual clocks from DCGM.
- Power limit: fixed per SKU (recorded), no dynamic power management features that add noise.
- CPU governor: performance
- Disable turbo if it adds variability for CPU-heavy phases (TBD; most inference is GPU-bound but tokenization/pipeline can matter for TTFT)

Observability + validation
Must-have metrics (per run, written into results artifact)
- Node ID + GPU UUIDs
- Driver + CUDA + runtime commit + container digest
- Actual GPU clocks + power limit
- GPU temperature (min/max)
- DCGM health status at start/end
- Kernel selection logging enabled only for benchmark runs (flagged) to avoid overhead in general.

Dashboards
- Tag convention: gpu_sku=h200, quant_mode=fp8|int8|fp16, model_family=llama|qwen|mistral, phase=prefill|decode
- Panels to add (Allison/Aisha owning):
  - TTFT p50/p95 by model/workload
  - TPOT p50/p95
  - tokens/sec
  - scheduler queue wait histograms (if enabled)
  - failure rate of nightly canary

Access controls
Principle: H200 pool is perf-lab critical path; keep access tight and auditable.

Cluster access
- Separate k8s namespace: perf-lab-h200
- RBAC groups:
  - perf-lab-h200-admin: SRE only (Sean, Allison)
  - perf-lab-h200-runner: benchmark owners + runtime perf folks (Rina, Noah, Grace, Yuki, Isabella)
  - perf-lab-h200-viewer: broader eng-runtime read-only (for dashboards/logs)
- Require SSO group membership for namespace access (no long-lived shared kubeconfigs).

Node access (SSH)
- SSH only via bastion with short-lived certificates.
- Allowlist users for direct node access (profiling only). Everyone else runs via jobs.
- Commands likely needed for profiling: nsight-systems/nsight-compute, nvidia-smi, dcgmi, perf collectors.
- All sessions logged (tty/auditd) and stored for 30 days.

Secrets + credentials
- Benchmark artifact uploads use service accounts with least privilege.
- Any S3/GCS keys via Vault (no plaintext in configs).

Data handling
- Prompts/workloads are internal benchmark sets (not customer data).
- Results artifacts are OK to store in shared engineering buckets/Drive, but must not include raw prompts if they contain licensed content. Prefer prompt IDs + hashes.

Capacity dependencies / asks
- INT-842: dedicated perf-lab capacity + contention mitigation.
- ENG-24813: expand GPU coverage to H200 + L40S (dependency: H200 nodes online).
- Need infra ops confirmation on:
  - rack/power availability for 4 nodes
  - IB switch ports
  - base image pipeline slot (packer/buildkite runner time)

Contingency plan (if H200 slips)
- Run the full matrix on H100/H200-lite subset if available.
- Use a single H200 node for microbench + kernel-level validation only; publish end-to-end serving metrics as “H100 baseline” with “H200 spot checks.”
- Clearly label in sprint report which cells are missing due to infra capacity.

Open questions
- Final driver/CUDA versions once the actual node SKU + firmware constraints are confirmed.
- Whether to standardize on CUDA-in-container only (preferred) vs CUDA on host for profiling tools.
- Whether to disable CPU turbo globally on H200 nodes.
- How many nodes we can reserve nightly for canary without impacting human-driven matrix runs.

Action items
- Sean: confirm node delivery / rack timeline + update this doc with exact dates (by 2025-10-01).
- Allison/Aisha: draft dashboard panels + alert routing for H200 canary (by 2025-10-04).
- Rina/Noah: confirm benchmark harness supports gpu_sku=h200 tagging + container digest pinning (by 2025-10-03).
- Connor: confirm release gating expectations for quant-perf canary on H200 vs H100 (by 2025-10-07).

Notes to self
- Biggest failure mode in the past: noisy neighbors + background jobs. Enforce exclusive reservations and kill any daemonsets that add jitter.
- Make sure benchmark artifact includes “node_contention_detected” flag if allocator sees overlapping reservations or high host load.
